newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee quietly higher by close on NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee quietly higher by close on NY.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures were higher by the close, boosted by renewed strength in New York but activity was thin and dominated by two-way arbitrage trades.

"It's mainly arbitrage dominated, selling and buying against New York," said one trader. By the close, second-position January firmed $10 to $1,394 after holding around $1,380 in the morning. Front-month November stood at $1,524, the same as Friday's close.
Up to midsession, values were weighed down by Asian origin selling. However light roaster buying helped prices to recover from their lows.
Traders said the market was awaiting latest U.S. certified stock data due to be released after New York's close on Monday.
But one said, "it doesn't really matter now as stocks are effectively zero anyway."
An error was made in the amount of coffee reduced from the certified stocks last week but there was no market reaction as the actual figure of just over 5,000 bags remaining was correct.
Traders said the market was unlikely to move unless stocks built up sharply.

Some traders expected a further draw in stocks while others said it could show a slight rise to reflect an adjustment following the reporting error. The latest weekly edition of the U.S. CFTC Commitment of Traders Report showed a slight increase in the net long positions by funds.
"The funds are still long and they have increased their longs slightly over the last week but they are going to start rolling their positions later in the week," said one trader.
"This should put the Dec/March spread in New York under pressure," he said.
Traders said the market was not overly concerned by the situation in Zaire where fighting between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops has uprooted half a million people.
"Zaire's coffee is not a considerable traded robusta any more," said one.

Supply/demand forecasts by the head of the International Coffee Organisation on Friday afternoon were within the lower end of trade expectations and had no immediate market impact. --Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
